simple.meaning: שְׂעַר (sᵉʻar) is a Hebrew word meaning “hair.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: שְׂעַר (H8177) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Daniel 3:27, with occurrences in Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שְׂעַר (H8177) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in שְׂעַר (H8177) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: שְׂעַר (sᵉʻar) / H8177 is traced through Daniel 3:27, Daniel 4:30, Daniel 7:9 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: The local governors, the deputies, and the governors, and the king’s counselors, being gathered together, saw these men, that the fire had no power on their bodies. The hair of their head wasn’t singed. Their pants weren’t changed, the smell of fire wasn’t even on them.

timeline.evidenceText: The local governors, the deputies, and the governors, and the king’s counselors, being gathered together, saw these men, that the fire had no power on their bodies. The hair of their head wasn’t singed. Their pants weren’t changed, the smell of fire wasn’t even on them.
The king spoke and said, “Is not this great Babylon, which I have built for the royal dwelling place, by the might of my power and for the glory of my majesty?”
